newsitem.title: POLAND: INVESTORS IN WARSAW SEEN FOCUSED ON NFIS NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: INVESTORS IN WARSAW SEEN FOCUSED ON NFIS NEXT WEEK.

text.p: The Thursday debut of Polish National Investment Funds (NFIs), seen as a milestone in the country's mass privatisation scheme, is likely to overshadow other events on the bourse next week, analysts said.
They said undergoing and forthcoming large privatisations were additionally drawing investor capital and attention from the bourse.
Analysts said the initial low liquidity of the NFIs might result in thin turnovers and rapid price swings on individual funds at the beginning of their bourse trade.

"It will be a symbolic event, but there is bound to be a period of low liquidity...there could be rapid, large price changes...and it might last a month or so," said Artur Kobos of ING Barings in Warsaw.
So far about 1.5 million mass privatisation units, out of a total of 26 million, were exchanged into 15 NFI shares each.

Analysts said the bourse may be further neglected next week by the undergoing sale of Poland's largest bank, Bank Handlowy SA, offering one-billion zlotys worth of shares and KGHM Polska Miedz SA, which later this month will offer shares worth at least 300 million zlotys in its domestic tranche.

Analysts said however that the bourse has some upward potential in the beginning of next week, after falling 2.2 percent since late last week, but that it would remain in its 2.5-month horizontal trend.
"I think there will still be stabilisation (on the market) but growth is quite likely on Monday," ING Baring's Kobos said.

Analysts said many investors were limiting buying ahead of Poland's parliamentary elections due in September, but said the country's good economic prospects such as growing GDP and falling inflation were preventing significant falls.
Some said the Warsaw bourse would stage a small rally at beginning of next week in the wake of all-time highs in other Central European bourses, such as the Budapest exchange.
A new Reuter poll of leading securities houses, relased for the first time on Friday, showed the Warsaw bourse's WIG index at just below 15,996 points at the end of this month.
The all-share main WIG index closed at 16,000.6 points on Friday, 0.4 percent higher than last week.
The week's top gainers on the main market were construction company Unibud which surged 25.9 percent and Zywiec which rose 16.4 percent.
The biggest losers were electrodes maker ZEW and PEPEES which fell 18.4 percent.
